html:
Roman emperor from 79 to 81 CE, the elder son of Vespasian and the general who destroyed Jerusalem. Despite that, the Romans remembered his short reign fondly.

In 67 he joined his father in the war against the Jewish revolt in Judea. When Vespasian left to claim the throne in 69, Titus took command. In 70 CE he besieged Jerusalem, and his troops burned the Second Temple (Romans destroy the Second Temple). The Arch of Titus in Rome still shows his soldiers carrying off the great menorah. Back in Rome he commanded his father's guard and had a long affair with the Judean queen Berenice, which the Romans disliked.

He became emperor in June 79. That year Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii and Herculaneum, and he sent help to the area. Pliny the Elder, who died in the eruption, had dedicated his Natural History to Titus. In 80 a great fire burned in Rome. That same year Titus opened the Colosseum, begun by his father, with a hundred days of games.

He died of a fever in 81, aged 41, and his brother Domitian took the throne.
